inventory_name: Hydrus reference GUI nested feature inventory

status_definitions.first_pass: Existing native behavior with documented/behavioral/oracle evidence; intentionally limited, never complete Qt parity.
status_definitions.partial: Native feature area exists with known omitted controls/workflows or meaningful behavior differences.
status_definitions.missing: Concrete Python feature exists and docs/native UI explicitly defer its native GUI or workflow. Runtime/preservation/interchange support may still exist.
status_definitions.unassessed: Reference feature found; precise native behavior/coverage not evaluated.

counting_rules: Nodes represent user-visible semantic features, dialogs and workflows rather than individual raw Qt widgets.
Feature_scope edges are organizational; direct_symbol edges give concrete parent-child mentions.
Shared references use target_id and should not count as independently implemented editors.
Descendant counts do not expand shared targets recursively and do not imply maximum modal stack depth. Nested/zipper formulas allow recursive nesting beyond this finite tree.
Use this selected inventory to navigate breadth and gaps; it is not an exhaustive whole-client coverage denominator.

Existing evidence filenames do not certify all controls; hosted validation is recorded separately for the overnight implementation checkpoint. Native module source anchors do not equate callbacks with parity.
unique_reachable_feature_count_including_shared expands shared editor targets once with cycle protection; useful for visualizer breadth, not a parity percentage.
Unique concrete-feature counts exclude root/menu/submenu and both family/feature_family organizational containers, plus target_id/canonical_editor aliases; aggregation schema concrete_features_v2.
limitations: Source-backed semantic hierarchy selected from Hydrus v688 GUI behavior, expanded through options/search/predicate, media/tagging/duplicates, service/database, network/import/export and shared-editor workflows.
Options include recorded labelled controls and nested option-list editors, with precise native exposure/ignored/unsupported distinctions; imported data preservation is not UI implementation.

Historical assessments retain their source-inspection provenance. Overnight implementation regressions passed hosted workspace CI. First-pass statuses identify supported slices and retain concrete limitations.
Dedicated advanced formula editing and date conversion execution are distinguished from runtime preservation/interchange support.
Menu labels/availability alone do not prove actions; unsupported dialogs and active no-op commands are represented as missing controls/workflows.
The finite map uses shared references for recursive editors and does not enumerate every widget/runtime state or assert a whole-client coverage denominator.

nodes.assessment: Both sides now use real count/domain/service-aware write autocomplete, typed/ideal elevation, parent and sibling decorations, visible-height preference, keyboard highlight/selected/click entry, manual fetch, confirmed or skipped multiline paste. Paste only adds and removes the entered tag from the opposite side; each service preserves independent input drafts. Closing owner invalidates pending paste answers and stale Apply. Shared favourites/children tabs now use the configured count service for favourites decorators and descendant/display-count ordering for children; selected tags are excluded and applied limit/show-all feeds existing inputs. Shared right-click native menus now copy raw tags/subtags/underscores/counts/parents/all rows, toggle per-widget/per-tab decorations, manage favourites and per-service most-used with exact removal questions and reread concurrent writes, and launch raw child predicates through a weak main-window hook. Pending menus block owner editing/Apply and owner close invalidates questions/callbacks. Menus now query all real service display graphs for grouped siblings/ideal/parent/child entries and open owned relationship editors seeded on every service tab; owner close cancels child. Relationship dialogs consume configured default/remember preferences and preserve staged cancellation separately from immediate service memory. Per-widget file/tag-domain buttons now have checked menus and exact all-known interlocks, preserve independent service drafts, feed real query/count/decorator/children consumers and use an owned staged multiple/deleted selector; cancelling does not write options or damage input domains. Shared logical multi-selection; plain/Ctrl/reversible Shift and Ctrl+Shift; inherited parent-row origin; unchanged fetch/decorations retain batch; Enter/double-click activates batch in ManageTags, both relationship sides and detached child. Cancel/reopen and stale callbacks retain staged owner boundaries. No new completed original-ID count. All recorded multi-tag local context paths: selected tags/subtags/underscores/counts/deduplicated parents clipboard copies, AND/OR/each-tag/duplicate native page launches, whole-selection relationship child seeds. Selected-tag maintenance records exact warning/title/buttons and repairs connected storage/display counts and subtag indexes across services/domains; preserves mappings/relations and unrelated caches; Cancel/stale owners discard pending answers. No new completed original-ID count. Accepted clipboard additions preserve caller text drafts and result selection. Declining the multiline question resumes native paste at retained cursor/selection, preserving raw newlines exactly; undo/redo restore recorded drafts. A small TextInput wrapper disables single-line only during paste, retaining native editor engine. Both relationship inputs, ManageTags and detached editors consume it; closed owners ignore pending answers. Real result-keyboard sequence: logical arrow wrapping; reversible Shift/Ctrl+Shift selection; Home/End endpoints; physical-row PageUp/PageDown including expanded parent rows; CtrlP/N; focused result CtrlA; ordered CtrlC and deduplicated parents on CtrlShiftC. Native selected editor text keeps its own copy engine. All three owner callbacks guard pending operations and closed owners; navigation keeps draft unchanged and scrolls to last hit. Focused Escape clears selected results without entering tags/changing draft/cancelling owner; second Escape propagates cancellation. All three native owner key-capture layers delegate after their popup/pending guards. A persistent non-repeated pointer surface records and consumes real press/move/release: range addition/reversal, inherited parent origin, Ctrl deselection start and reversible removal/restoration. Pointer handlers survive replaced suggestions models. Each input owns replacement history: paste is atomic; caret movement, intervening Undo/Redo and changed deletion direction split commands, while adjacent typing/same-direction deletion coalesces. Fresh edits invalidate redo; Unicode selection replay converts recorded Qt UTF16 units to native UTF8 byte offsets. Recorded replacement selection/owner isolation remains separate from the broader shared input.

The native grid keeps the saved grid role behind viewport margins and the bottom-right background-image layer. This covers represented native grid integration; QColorDialog topology, QSS/OS palettes and unrepresented controls remain outside scope. No dedicated combined saved-role-plus-background-bitmap pixel-parity claim is made.
Linux only at exact9bec source; Windows/macOS deferred. Only this original concrete ID earns credit; no structural parent/alias or unrelated thumbnail-option completion.

reference_source.symbol: rows.append( ( 'When maintenance physically deletes files, wait this long between each delete:

nodes.assessment: Actual Qt seconds/milliseconds fields default to 600 ms, clamp minimum 20 ms, and have 59/999 field maxima. Cancel retains raw imported milliseconds; unchanged Apply accepts displayed fields once without overwriting a concurrent policy, and explicit edits preserve their actual float-sum conversion (1 s 29 ms saves 1029 ms and reopens at 1 s 28 ms). Native-wins retained ClientOptions load, future import, field-scoped save and hidden/retired controls reach the real maintenance consumer. Each pass snapshots its saved delay; each admitted file/thumbnail pair commits its durable queue clear then waits outside the writer, including the final pair and a missing original. Successors recheck current queue/membership/shared-media/import claims. Restored local media only clears an inconsistent queue and does not perform or wait for a physical pair; actual reference re-add clears those queues before the loop. Owned worker shutdown wakes bounded waits, retires further admissions and joins on normal shutdown. Failed pairs remain queued and receive no successful-pair wait; earlier pairs stay committed. Broader maintenance parents remain Partial.

nodes.label: When finishing archive/delete filtering, delay activation of multiple deletion choice buttons:

reference_source.symbol: delay activation of multiple deletion choice buttons:

nodes.assessment: Independent saved true-default checkbox disables all genuinely multiple deletion commit buttons for exactly1.2seconds; single-choice/all-domains and keep-only finishes are immediately available. Disabling the saved policy reaches the next finish immediately; staged Cancel/Apply/reopen and scoped concurrent field merge preserve other settings.

nodes.label: Remove files from view when they are sent to the trash:
nodes.assessment: Default-false exact checkbox stages, imports legacy remove_trashed_files and affects live native simple/advanced thumbnail/viewer deletion and filter content events after Apply. Source-page callbacks cannot target a successor and retained rows invalidate stale inbox/trash icons.

Hidden/retired Options cannot stage/save, declined exit preserves live work, successor owners consume the remaining real queue. Broader maintenance parents remain Partial. A private Bound Owner makes final binding-clone retirement immediate despite retained Main callbacks/public Control; the dropped Main is discovered by its weak timer/poll.

Owned precision reaches page totals, bandwidth status/review/jobs/rules/graphs, file-info hover/status/menu sizes and bitrate, local-import size rows, service totals, import-option/default/favourite summaries, parser/formula raw preview labels, PNG descriptions, live importer/download-review and popup progress. Reference half-even rounding retains whole digits and sub-KB integer wording. Download progress preserves gauges, status first lines and cancellation ownership for quick/unknown-total/zero/error cases. FileImporter uses current saved precision for actual min/max/GIF size rejection and critical-drive diagnostics, with the original import-family pause persistence. Both whole-response and range-chunk over-length failures read the engine’s saved precision after settings reload. Existing low-level validation APIs keep their default-three-figure compatibility; saved owning consumers call explicit precision overloads.

nodes.label: When there are too many tabs to fit, '...' elide their names so they fit:
nodes.assessment: The page tab names checkbox stages/persists/imports/reopens with default true. The actual native tab label uses measured glyph widths and per-input fitting state to paint a middle ellipsis only when overflow requires it; the stored/decorated label and full tooltip remain unchanged. Disabled elision keeps complete label text in the scrolling strip; small overflow arrows preserve label height and reserve a trailing area so the final tab can be exposed at maximum scroll. Both horizontal and vertical bars consume the flag, including nested notebooks. The overflow probe uses the same selected600/unselected400 glyph weights as the painted tab, so a near-fit selected name triggers fitting rather than mistakenly scrolling.

nodes.label: Always Loop Animations:
nodes.assessment: Exact Always Loop Animations checkbox defaulttrue stages until Apply, persists and imports always_loop_gifs. Native animation players in media viewer/archive-delete/duplicate filters read the preference at each wrap and honor file play counts when false, pausing on the final frame after the stored count. Stored0 and ugoira mean infinite; missing GIF loop metadata means1. The existing mpv consumer captures GIF/APNG metadata at file load, pauses/seeks to start after the finite restart count and uses newly applied preference on the next load. Slideshow stop remains independent. Fresh actual Qt decoding/painting/timer output covers stored0/1/2 with forced looping on/off; separate real GIF/APNG reads cover finite/infinite/absent metadata. Tests cover controls, migration, decoded-native finite pause/live changes, owned viewer final-frame stability/resume, Cancel/reopen and existing MPV backend when available.

The MPV regression runs only where libmpv is available, as existing player tests do; metadata parsing and native decoded-frame regressions are unconditional. Existing MPV restart polling behavior is retained. Enabling looping does not resume already paused media, matching the reference.

nodes.label: FFMPEG call timeout:
nodes.assessment: Stage actual media playback/system timeout1..600/default15. Cancel/hidden/retired callbacks leave saved policy unchanged; Apply/reopen persists and normalizes imported raw bounds without clobbering independent fields or a newer implicit-normalization target. Native saved value wins over retained ClientOptions; real legacy importer decodes the value. FileImporter installs weak Store policy into MediaTools/Ffmpeg, reaching real imports/downloader imports/maintenance and thumbnail regeneration. Paste image! uses configured tools, including ffmpeg-only image formats. The common weak reader also reaches Review MIME detection, StoreContent duplicate comparison/auto-resolution decodes, parser fetched-file detection and import-folder sidecar samples, preserving old standalone no-Store APIs. About version now uses same timed process path and preserves existing scheduling/absent UI. Capture deadline once before subprocess spawn; later Apply affects next process only. Three-second adapter preserves recorded polling outcomes while explicit fixed timeout and stream ownership remain intact. Existing bounded backend kills/waits before returning.

limitations: Actual reference consumers execute an authored local delayed executable through unchanged HydrusFFMPEG and HydrusSubprocess. This proves saved timeout/capture/poll semantics, not codec correctness or external network. Native FIFO transports are distinct native regression inputs.

Saved preference adapter captures ceil(clamp(n,1,600)/3)*3 seconds per bounded process, matching observed three-second polling outcomes. The native monotonic precise backend can differ by scheduler/termination overhead from Qt wall-clock strict-passed polling; raw imported values remain saved until Apply while effective execution bounds malformed inputs.

Explicit Ffmpeg::timeout(Duration) precision is preserved and overrides the saved reader. Streaming reads retain existing fixed per-chunk timeout and Drop kill/wait; streaming/player-reuse/executable-selection controls remain unclaimed.

limitations: Only the selected original frozen thumbnail-cache controls are in scope; the independent Debug clear-thumbnail action remains deferred. Speed and Memory, thumbnail-cache and Help/debug parents remain Partial; no alias/new ID, image/tile/prefetch/video cache or other debug action is counted.

Reference ThumbnailCache is process-wide. Native cache is owned by one main GUI incarnation and shared across its pages; separate main windows do not share raster entries. Apply updates the currently owned cache immediately. Rebind and accepted exit retire rows and cancel their staged Options owner, while declined exit preserves both.

Native cache accounts decoded RGB/RGBA buffer bytes and 128 bytes for a missing-thumbnail entry. Reference HydrusBitmap may store compressed data. Renderer-held image clones, loader queues, metadata/icon caches and total process/GPU memory are outside this finite accounted budget. As in reference, admission may overflow by one incoming entry until maintenance; this is not a hard total-memory ceiling.

Timeout uses monotonic last access and strict older-than expiry. Existing 25ms owned main collection ticks perform maintenance without requiring a new thumbnail request. Native inline day/hour/minute editing preserves untouched raw 299 seconds and enforces 300 seconds once edited; the reference duration-popup geometry remains outside this slice.
Linux-only validation at the exact source/run/artifact; Windows and macOS are deferred. Approval covers this original leaf only, with no broader parent, alias or unrelated completion credit.

All eight fresh shared helper PNGs were actually inspected. Estimates, warnings and numeric controls are separate at all four sizes, including the wrapped long warning; lower rows fall below the normal ScrollView fold. Shared layout evidence does not widen the defining consumer claim.
The reference ThumbnailCache is process-wide. The native cache belongs to one Main incarnation and is shared across its pages; separate Main windows do not share entries.

The accounted budget includes owned decoded RGB/RGBA pixels and 128-byte missing entries. Renderer-held clones, loader queues, metadata/icon caches and total process/GPU memory are outside this budget; reference HydrusBitmap may compress.

Admission permits one incoming entry beyond the soft byte budget until maintenance. This is not a hard total-memory ceiling. Strict monotonic last-access expiry runs through the existing 25 ms collection maintenance, and saved policy changes apply immediately.

Native inline day/hour/minute editing differs from the Qt duration popup. Untouched raw 299 seconds remains 299; edited fields clamp to at least 300 seconds. B through TB amount/unit cases replay in model/store tests; native GUI assertions cover representative cases.
The separate Help/debug clear-thumbnail-cache leaf is excluded even though this shared suite records and exercises it; this review gives it no independent action, menu or parity approval.

limitations: Only the three frozen original concrete image-cache controls are in scope for these assessments. Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, image-tile, video buffers and global backend parity remain Partial with zero extra credit; no aliases or structural completions. The separate prefetch-per-viewer percentage is reviewed independently and receives no credit from these three image-cache assessments.

Qt uses a controller-global ImageRendererCache. Native owns one cache per Main binding incarnation, shared by its real preview, still viewer, archive/delete and duplicate filter; standalone duplicate filters own separate policy-bound caches. Final Bound-clone drop, rebind and accepted close permanently retire admission while retained worker/callback handles cannot revive it.

Full still-image cache bytes are pending metadata RGB estimates and loaded RGB/RGBA raster bytes recounted at access. The cache admits one incoming item above its soft bound until maintenance, matching Qt. Pending decoders, accepted per-page 64MiB preview snapshots, current canvas/source/resize buffers, Slint image copies, playback and total process/GPU memory are separate presentation/resource ownership and are not evicted or counted as cache bytes.

Percentage uses strict estimated-size admission and applies only to future misses; existing admitted renderers remain subject to ordinary byte/idle maintenance. Saved policy and ICC changes refresh without resetting current accepted media, zoom, generation/page identity or viewing intervals. Future duplicate copies can only reuse cache-owned full rasters, while the current presentation remains independently retained.

Failed full-image and non-image thumbnail/poster fallback remain uncached; decoder injection keeps the public preview Decoder contract and bypasses the production cache. Existing worker bounds and late-publication generation guards are retained. Imported partial resolution falls back to100x100 exactly; real media metadata/ICC identity displaces stale cached sources.

Inline native duration fields preserve untouched raw299 seconds and enforce the actual300-second edit minimum; the Qt duration-popup geometry is a separate presentation difference. Monitor screen estimates use the owning physical monitor converted to logical size; headless windows without a monitor omit that caption rather than invent screen dimensions.
Validation is Linux only at this exact source and run; Windows and macOS are explicitly deferred, not passed.

The Qt PNGs have different staged values, accordion states and framework/font geometry from the final native states. This review confirms scoped readable controls, ordering and reference behavior; it does not claim pixel parity.

Exactly the six selected concrete controls receive review credit. Structural parents, general renderer/backend/tile/video/playback families and the separate duplicate-pair-count control retain broader Partial scope and zero extra credit.

All ten fresh native captures and both Qt PNGs were actually inspected. The unchanged strict finite/positive/bounds/positive-gap/long-warning geometry assertions passed. At 900px, long labels and the warning wrap readably; lower unselected controls remain scrollable rather than all-visible evidence.
The primary image shows saved cache=100B, timeout=5 minutes and storage=50%; its default previous=2, next=3, percentage=25% and pairs=3 are distinct from the saved prefetch producer.

publication_policy.reason: The owner uses Linux and prioritizes validated Linux delivery. macOS is low priority; Windows is deferred because its builds materially lengthen validation. Secondary-platform CI remains available by explicit opt-in.

nodes.label: Image cache timeout:
nodes.assessment: Actual days/hours/minutes duration stages/imports/persists/reopens seconds with300-second edited minimum, retaining untouched raw299. Strict monotonic idle expiry preserves equality and expires only older access, with owned periodic maintenance and immediate saved size/timeout refresh. Pending→loaded recount occurs at access; evicting or shortening timeout releases cache ownership while accepted media/current pixels/viewing intervals remain independent. Cancel and captured modal/lifetime guards apply.

limitations: Only the three frozen original concrete prefetch controls are in scope. Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, prefetch/shared renderer backend families, tile/video/cache-delay and the separate duplicate-pair-count control receive zero credit.

The represented GeneralImage full-resolution raster path admits only the effective supported native static-image display action. Qt global renderer/controller ownership, image-project/unsupported codecs, tile/GPU/video renderer prefetch remain broader Partial boundaries.

One lazily started worker per viewer owner admits at most one real miss per readiness pass and coalesces one latest pending navigation. Saved policy and ICC/candidate-action changes capture a new navigation generation. Cache finished-image notifications resume the same captured generation, including another owner’s completion, without publishing SetMedia or viewing intervals. Idle/pending waits hold no Store; in-flight existing disk IO retains its Store until completion and is never joined on the UI.

Current native rendering reuses ready shared Arc rasters but performs its pre-existing synchronous decode independently while warm work is pending. Duplicate overlap decode remains a broader renderer architecture difference from Qt shared asynchronous current-renderer objects; it does not evade the warm budget or count presentation references as cache bytes.

Current image prefix and circular wrap duplicates count their ready actual bytes exactly as Qt. Unknown-resolution misses abort; refusal blocks later small candidates. Total/single prefetch thresholds allow equality, cache admission remains strict, and an uncached successful equality decode repeats on readiness. Atomic easy-space flushing scans only finished entries and deletes none when strict free-space > incoming estimate cannot be reached.

Hidden viewers may continue admitted warm work, as real Qt Canvas does. Close/replacement/rebind/accepted Main close and final Bound-clone drop retire admission; retained GUI/cache handles cannot revive it. Current pixels/zoom/viewing intervals and accepted preview-page snapshots remain independently owned.

Decode failures retain existing native blank/fallback behavior rather than creating Qt error-placeholder renderers. Public preview Decoder injection, two-worker publication bounds, late page/generation guards and ICC identity remain unchanged. Duplicate count is imported/defaulted for this percentage consumer only; no duplicate-count Options row or leaf credit is added.
No physical-display or wider platform parity is inferred from headless Linux native execution; Windows/macOS validation remains deferred under the exact-source owner policy.
Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, prefetch/shared renderer backend families, tile/video/cache-delay and the separate duplicate-pair-count control receive zero credit.
Validation is Linux only at this exact source and run; Windows and macOS are explicitly deferred, not passed.

The Qt PNGs have different staged values, accordion states and framework/font geometry from the final native states. This review confirms scoped readable controls, ordering and reference behavior; it does not claim pixel parity.

Exactly the six selected concrete controls receive review credit. Structural parents, general renderer/backend/tile/video/playback families and the separate duplicate-pair-count control retain broader Partial scope and zero extra credit.

All ten fresh native captures and both Qt PNGs were actually inspected. The unchanged strict finite/positive/bounds/positive-gap/long-warning geometry assertions passed. At 900px, long labels and the warning wrap readably; lower unselected controls remain scrollable rather than all-visible evidence.

The primary image shows saved previous=1, next=1 and percentage=50%, with cache=400B. The eight helper captures intentionally show default previous=2, next=3 and percentage=25%; they supplement geometry rather than replace saved-state proof. Both actual producers retain default duplicate_pairs=3 and supply no pair-count credit.

publication_policy.reason: The owner uses Linux and prioritizes validated Linux delivery. macOS is low priority; Windows is deferred because its builds materially lengthen validation. Secondary-platform CI remains available by explicit opt-in.

limitations: Only the three frozen original concrete prefetch controls are in scope. Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, prefetch/shared renderer backend families, tile/video/cache-delay and the separate duplicate-pair-count control receive zero credit.

The represented GeneralImage full-resolution raster path admits only the effective supported native static-image display action. Qt global renderer/controller ownership, image-project/unsupported codecs, tile/GPU/video renderer prefetch remain broader Partial boundaries.

One lazily started worker per viewer owner admits at most one real miss per readiness pass and coalesces one latest pending navigation. Saved policy and ICC/candidate-action changes capture a new navigation generation. Cache finished-image notifications resume the same captured generation, including another owner’s completion, without publishing SetMedia or viewing intervals. Idle/pending waits hold no Store; in-flight existing disk IO retains its Store until completion and is never joined on the UI.

Current native rendering reuses ready shared Arc rasters but performs its pre-existing synchronous decode independently while warm work is pending. Duplicate overlap decode remains a broader renderer architecture difference from Qt shared asynchronous current-renderer objects; it does not evade the warm budget or count presentation references as cache bytes.

Current image prefix and circular wrap duplicates count their ready actual bytes exactly as Qt. Unknown-resolution misses abort; refusal blocks later small candidates. Total/single prefetch thresholds allow equality, cache admission remains strict, and an uncached successful equality decode repeats on readiness. Atomic easy-space flushing scans only finished entries and deletes none when strict free-space > incoming estimate cannot be reached.

Hidden viewers may continue admitted warm work, as real Qt Canvas does. Close/replacement/rebind/accepted Main close and final Bound-clone drop retire admission; retained GUI/cache handles cannot revive it. Current pixels/zoom/viewing intervals and accepted preview-page snapshots remain independently owned.

Decode failures retain existing native blank/fallback behavior rather than creating Qt error-placeholder renderers. Public preview Decoder injection, two-worker publication bounds, late page/generation guards and ICC identity remain unchanged. Duplicate count is imported/defaulted for this percentage consumer only; no duplicate-count Options row or leaf credit is added.
No physical-display or wider platform parity is inferred from headless Linux native execution; Windows/macOS validation remains deferred under the exact-source owner policy.

The Qt PNGs have different staged values, accordion states and framework/font geometry from the final native states. This review confirms scoped readable controls, ordering and reference behavior; it does not claim pixel parity.

Exactly the six selected concrete controls receive review credit. Structural parents, general renderer/backend/tile/video/playback families and the separate duplicate-pair-count control retain broader Partial scope and zero extra credit.

All ten fresh native captures and both Qt PNGs were actually inspected. The unchanged strict finite/positive/bounds/positive-gap/long-warning geometry assertions passed. At 900px, long labels and the warning wrap readably; lower unselected controls remain scrollable rather than all-visible evidence.

The primary image shows saved previous=1, next=1 and percentage=50%, with cache=400B. The eight helper captures intentionally show default previous=2, next=3 and percentage=25%; they supplement geometry rather than replace saved-state proof. Both actual producers retain default duplicate_pairs=3 and supply no pair-count credit.

nodes.label: EXPERIMENTAL: Minimum gallery importer update time:

reference_source.symbol: EXPERIMENTAL: Minimum gallery importer update time:

nodes.assessment: Exact independent staged gallery seconds/milliseconds minimum with a 250 ms lower bound and 59 s/999 ms constructor fields; reference defaults 1000 ms/30, typed raw legacy import, cancelled/retained Apply rejection, unchanged constructor-bound acceptance, field-scoped concurrent merge and save/reopen. Saved values reach the real visible current-page gallery list/totals scheduler: every 250 ms GUI tick checks strict now>pending deadline, samples displayed row count before refresh, sets next=now+max(minimum_ms/1000,rows/denominator), uses 1 s zero-denominator fallback, and force refresh resets the deadline to 0. Saved changes preserve the pending deadline and affect the next period. Highlighted jobs/tab progress/close eligibility stay live separately. Same-binding tab roundtrips retain offscreen/pre-deadline snapshots and refresh overdue returns. Hidden owners skip reads; rebind and accepted close permanently reject old retained refresh/sync, including close/re-show; cancelled close stays live.

nodes.label: Favourite tag list editor
nodes.assessment: The Tag autocomplete tabs / favourite tags page opens the shared write-tag editor for all-known tags. It starts from the parent options draft; manual choices and pasted tags only add (repeated additions retain existing tags), explicit removal deletes, and rows/save order use natural text order. Child Apply updates the parent draft without a store write. Child Cancel preserves that draft; parent Cancel and window close discard accepted unsaved lists and invalidate child callbacks. Parent Apply waits for any open favourite editor, writes only changed settings, persists/reopens the list, preserves unrelated concurrent settings and feeds every shared favourites tab, including a real native Manage Tags consumer.

Admitted requests copy geometry and recovery policy; failed stored-thumbnail/regeneration loads decode retained FileInfo.blurhash using the actual reference component/gamma/base83 rules, 32x32 recovery wrapper and reference resizing. Invalid/absent/disabled values publish the bundled default without physical regeneration or metadata writes. Saved toggle invalidates the cache and rejects held old generations before pending/cache mutation; real missing-original/thumbnail native replay keeps valid source metadata before false Apply and asserts different default pixels. Current physical storage membership distinguishes local/remote normal/selected paints; palette invalidation clears both current and previous fade snapshots without changing decoded thumbnail bytes/cache entries. This covers represented native grid integration; QColorDialog topology, QSS/OS palettes and unrepresented controls remain outside scope. No dedicated combined saved-role-plus-background-bitmap pixel-parity claim is made.
Linux only at exact9bec source; Windows/macOS deferred. Only this original concrete ID earns credit; no structural parent/alias or unrelated thumbnail-option completion.

Native opening/minimum measurements use physical1x software-rendered client areas. OS compositor minimum enforcement, HiDPI native window behavior and broad font/platform pixel parity are not established.

Qt picker PNG uses19/83/197 and full QColorDialog topology; native picker capture uses the initial255/255/255 role. Qt Colours PNG showsdefault/default, native enabled capture intentionallyshowsdarkmode/darkmode after physical input. These are related different states, not paired bitmap parity.

Role-paint exports deliberately isolate thumbnail/viewer paint in places; controlled fade-clock and250ms observer evidence do not establish full compositor or arbitrary scheduling parity.

nodes.label: Search predicate undo history

native_source.description: Inspected this native subsystem and its callbacks; Reference keeps added/removed predicate batches and builds addition/removal submenus; native SearchPage enters/removes predicates without a matching undo-history model.

nodes.assessment: Frame-owned, transient, separate deduplicated addition/removal recency lists populate the actual searching submenus newest first. Typed stable commands toggle the selected historical predicate on the currently visible media page, retire its entry before recording the resulting delta, and leave stale commands inert. New/restored page predicates do not enter history; histories survive page close/restore, apply across pages and stay independent across windows. Committed typed OR is one entry; cancelled predicate children and refused inputs add none. Undo enters a locked page hidden query while retaining its lock; with an empty notebook selected, it preserves history. Clear history uses the exact reference confirmation: rejection retains both lists; acceptance clears both without changing searches or closed-page history. History names use raw predicate text despite hidden-namespace presentation. Populated locked pages retain their prior lock badge and media even with synchronization enabled; locking and hash synchronization update the cached panel count. Accepted system values preserve originating Shift intent: drafts extend without frame history; normal activation merges into one committed OR history entry. Accepting a system value and later cancelling its outer OR leaves frame history unchanged while retaining actual reference recent predicates.

evidence.description: Inspected this native subsystem and its callbacks; Reference keeps added/removed predicate batches and builds addition/removal submenus; native SearchPage enters/removes predicates without a matching undo-history model.

Within one multi-predicate delta, native recency follows deterministic predicate order; reference Python set-difference ordering can vary across processes. Single-entry and cross-event recency, recorded batch outputs, and canonical identities are covered by authored replay.

nodes.label: close and reload current gui session
nodes.assessment: Exact Help/debug/gui action freezes the current ordered tree, files and importer options/logs, asynchronously commits/loads a private immutable Store snapshot, removes its slot, then forcibly closes the current pages without a question and reconstructs fresh page and importer identities. Actual Qt first-root/first-child selection and empty-thumbnail-selection reset are retained. Closed original pages remain undoable with original queues paused; restored queues start fresh and retain captured settings/logs. Later edits/new pages cannot alter the admitted snapshot. Hidden new requests are refused but admitted work delivers while Main is hidden. Weak Main/Pages and weak timer callbacks, permanent binding retirement and shared final-Bound-clone lease reject late completions after accepted exit/rebind/final-clone/Main destruction; Exit Cancel preserves admitted work.

limitations: Native unique private snapshot rows are not exposed as saved session names; Qt uses a fixed temporary named session. Overlapping native captures therefore cannot overwrite one another.
The existing synchronous snapshot-capture and final restore/close Store boundaries remain on the UI thread; broader large-session responsiveness is outside this debug action.
Already-running Store work finishes and removes its slot after retirement; its reply cannot replace pages. Native IO diagnostics use the existing main-window note instead of the Qt exception popup.
Manual save-last-session, wider session/debug GUI/style families and parent/alias nodes receive no credit.

Qt screenshot is post-reload first-root locked2-files search with tags and no displayed thumbnails; native export follows same reload consumer with decoded thumbnails. Compare tab names/first selection and legible controls, not whole-frame geometry or identical thumbnail capture timing. Native unique private slots differ from fixed Qt temporary name.

nodes.assessment: Add genuine Help > debug > gui actions > make a new page in five seconds between existing long-text and delayed-popup actions. Its immutable menu command captures resolved typed default local file location at menu construction; each invocation enqueues a separate five-second monotonic page request, no early page creation. At delivery create/select a real blank query in the current notebook through existing ChangePages/Pages/SearchPage path, reading current saved tag-service default. Temporarily detach and then restore any live chooser destination/depth so the background page cannot consume its captured root/notebook/insertion anchor. Actual query and result thumbnails use the live Store. Overlapping launches retain their locations/deadlines; hidden Main existing work proceeds without raising it, while hidden new launch is refused. Share existing weak single-shot earliest deadline/200ms liveness queue with long and delayed popups, preserving all long updates, dismissal pruning and popup publication. Exit Cancel preserves work; accepted exit/rebind/Bound destruction/lost Main permanently clear requests, timer and captured consumer; retained controls cannot resurrect work.

Native owned-clock launch offsets0/1000 and deadlines5000/6000 are separate deterministic authored inputs, not claims of physically executed native five-second timers.

Qt Help construction retains its default local LocationContext; native Help/menu construction captures the resolved full typed location. Delivery selects the notebook current then and reads the current saved tag default, preserving existing all-known-file/tag fallback and normal query infrastructure. Native independently opening menus can rebuild facts more often than the reference cached Help menu; the captured active menu payload itself is immutable through trigger/delivery.

Merely hidden Main receives existing work without being raised; new native GUI invocation while hidden is refused. Real Qt minimized delivery was recorded, while backend-specific native minimized state remains a hosted/platform limit. Native accepted-exit/rebind/destruction permanently disposes pending requests more strongly than independent Qt backend callbacks.

limitations: Only the original clear-thumbnail-cache action is in scope. Speed and Memory, thumbnail-cache and Help/debug parents remain Partial; no alias/new ID, image/tile/prefetch/video cache or other debug action receives credit from this action.

Reference ThumbnailCache is process-wide. Native cache is owned by one main GUI incarnation and shared across its pages; separate main windows do not share raster entries. Apply updates the currently owned cache immediately. Rebind and accepted exit retire rows and cancel their staged Options owner, while declined exit preserves both.

Native cache accounts decoded RGB/RGBA buffer bytes and 128 bytes for a missing-thumbnail entry. Reference HydrusBitmap may store compressed data. Renderer-held image clones, loader queues, metadata/icon caches and total process/GPU memory are outside this finite accounted budget. As in reference, admission may overflow by one incoming entry until maintenance; this is not a hard total-memory ceiling.

Timeout uses monotonic last access and strict older-than expiry. Existing 25ms owned main collection ticks perform maintenance without requiring a new thumbnail request. Native inline day/hour/minute editing preserves untouched raw 299 seconds and enforces 300 seconds once edited; the reference duration-popup geometry remains outside this slice.

No recorded Qt PNG shows the clear-action menu or post-clear state. The source-grounded reference QAction recording proves clear_thumbnail_cache plus notify_complete_thumbnail_reset and empty cache keys; fresh native menu/reload stills plus unchanged reset/generation/owner regressions support this action, without pixel parity. Historical Qt cache Options at 1 day and native saved 5 minutes are different fixture states.

The visible nearby clear-all-rendering-caches entry receives no credit from this action. The native key callback route is exercised with real rendered menu placement; this evidence does not claim every OS input or all Help/debug menu behavior.

nodes.assessment: Replaced capped storage suggestions with shared zero-count aware, domain/service aware write search; raw/ideal elevation, counts, parent/sibling decorations, click/highlight entry, manual fetch, multiline/add-only clipboard questions and height controls. Shared favourites/children tabs now use the configured count service for favourites decorators and descendant/display-count ordering for children; selected tags are excluded and applied limit/show-all feeds existing inputs. Shared right-click native menus now copy raw tags/subtags/underscores/counts/parents/all rows, toggle per-widget/per-tab decorations, manage favourites and per-service most-used with exact removal questions and reread concurrent writes, and launch raw child predicates through a weak main-window hook. Pending menus block owner editing/Apply and owner close invalidates questions/callbacks. Menus now query all real service display graphs for grouped siblings/ideal/parent/child entries and open owned relationship editors seeded on every service tab; owner close cancels child. Relationship dialogs consume configured default/remember preferences and preserve staged cancellation separately from immediate service memory. Per-widget file/tag-domain buttons now have checked menus and exact all-known interlocks, preserve independent service drafts, feed real query/count/decorator/children consumers and use an owned staged multiple/deleted selector; cancelling does not write options or damage input domains. Shared logical multi-selection; plain/Ctrl/reversible Shift and Ctrl+Shift; inherited parent-row origin; unchanged fetch/decorations retain batch; Enter/double-click activates batch in ManageTags, both relationship sides and detached child. Cancel/reopen and stale callbacks retain staged owner boundaries. No new completed original-ID count. All recorded multi-tag local context paths: selected tags/subtags/underscores/counts/deduplicated parents clipboard copies, AND/OR/each-tag/duplicate native page launches, whole-selection relationship child seeds. Selected-tag maintenance records exact warning/title/buttons and repairs connected storage/display counts and subtag indexes across services/domains; preserves mappings/relations and unrelated caches; Cancel/stale owners discard pending answers. No new completed original-ID count. Accepted clipboard additions preserve caller text drafts and result selection. Declining the multiline question resumes native paste at retained cursor/selection, preserving raw newlines exactly; undo/redo restore recorded drafts. A small TextInput wrapper disables single-line only during paste, retaining native editor engine. Both relationship inputs, ManageTags and detached editors consume it; closed owners ignore pending answers. Real result-keyboard sequence: logical arrow wrapping; reversible Shift/Ctrl+Shift selection; Home/End endpoints; physical-row PageUp/PageDown including expanded parent rows; CtrlP/N; focused result CtrlA; ordered CtrlC and deduplicated parents on CtrlShiftC. Native selected editor text keeps its own copy engine. All three owner callbacks guard pending operations and closed owners; navigation keeps draft unchanged and scrolls to last hit. Focused Escape clears selected results without entering tags/changing draft/cancelling owner; second Escape propagates cancellation. All three native owner key-capture layers delegate after their popup/pending guards. A persistent non-repeated pointer surface records and consumes real press/move/release: range addition/reversal, inherited parent origin, Ctrl deselection start and reversible removal/restoration. Pointer handlers survive replaced suggestions models. Each input owns replacement history: paste is atomic; caret movement, intervening Undo/Redo and changed deletion direction split commands, while adjacent typing/same-direction deletion coalesces. Fresh edits invalidate redo; Unicode selection replay converts recorded Qt UTF16 units to native UTF8 byte offsets. Recorded replacement selection/owner isolation remains separate from the broader shared input.

nodes.label: Per-service additional tags / parse threshold
nodes.assessment: Per-service import additional tags open a detached write-tag child using that service; whitelist uses all known tags. Typed entry toggles, paste only adds, duplicate pastes retain existing tags. Accepted lists update only the captured parent draft field; cancelling child or owner discards edits, native child close unlocks parent, pending child blocks parent Apply. Shared favourites/children tabs now use the configured count service for favourites decorators and descendant/display-count ordering for children; selected tags are excluded and applied limit/show-all feeds existing inputs. Shared right-click native menus now copy raw tags/subtags/underscores/counts/parents/all rows, toggle per-widget/per-tab decorations, manage favourites and per-service most-used with exact removal questions and reread concurrent writes, and launch raw child predicates through a weak main-window hook. Pending menus block owner editing/Apply and owner close invalidates questions/callbacks. Menus now query all real service display graphs for grouped siblings/ideal/parent/child entries and open owned relationship editors seeded on every service tab; owner close cancels child. Relationship dialogs consume configured default/remember preferences and preserve staged cancellation separately from immediate service memory. Per-widget file/tag-domain buttons now have checked menus and exact all-known interlocks, preserve independent service drafts, feed real query/count/decorator/children consumers and use an owned staged multiple/deleted selector; cancelling does not write options or damage input domains.
limitations: Maintenance/admin actions and multiple-tag selection menus remain outstanding. Native tab dropdown/layout differs from Qt; multiple/deleted selector exposes existing native advanced domain ticks to preserve combined-domain choices. Existing parent leaf remains partial.
